title: Concrete Pump Blockage: Causes, Prevention and Safe Response
seoTitle: Concrete Pump Blockage Causes and Safe Response | Pinjin
description: Prevent trailer-pump blockages with mix, pipeline and wash-down practice from the Xingtai daily checklist. If a plug forms, ACPA requires relieving line pressure before opening the system and forbids compressed air to force a blockage.

answerBlock.what: A blockage (plug) is concrete that has stopped moving in the valve, reducer or pipeline. Prevention on Pinjin trailers is the Xingtai daily checklist: hopper, clamps, leaks, S-valve observation, after-pour wash. If a plug forms, the American Concrete Pumping Association (ACPA) instructs operators to reverse-pump to relieve line pressure, locate the plug, and remove the section by hand. Never use compressed air to remove a blockage.
answerBlock.who: Operators and site leads running trailer concrete pumps who need a sourced safety sequence, not a homemade air-blow trick.
factors: Mix stability and max aggregate versus pipe DN (see ACI 304.2R-17 and the Pinjin aggregate page)
Clamps, gaskets and pipeline support before the first load
Hopper not sucked empty (air in the line)
ACPA: relieve pressure, never compressed air on a plug

faqs.question: Can I blow a pipeline blockage out with an air compressor?
faqs.answer: No. ACPA’s safety alert states: never use compressed air to remove a blockage. Air stores energy; a concrete pump already produces far higher pressure than a typical compressor. Relieve line pressure by reverse pumping, then remove the plugged section.

faqs.question: Does Pinjin publish a blockage-hour table or a guaranteed unplug method?
faqs.answer: No. We publish a daily checklist and we cite ACPA for the pressure-release rule. Mix, pipe and yesterday’s wash change wear. Photograph the valve and pipe and send the model slug to the Xingtai factory.
